highlights.text: a "sound" root — a single, unified word rather than one built from overlapping senses
al-ṣakhrah — a huge, massive rock
The shared sense is settling into stillness and calm.
of a place, to become settled, still, and at rest
single root with one meaning: taking hold of something by force, domination, and strength
"Indeed the grip (baṭsh) of your Lord is severe" (al-Burūj 85:12)
al-baght: a thing happening suddenly, coming upon a person by surprise / unawares (yafjaʾ)
the sudden onset takes you unawares
a single underlying sense: driving away and pushing off to a distance
"Go out from it, disgraced and driven away (مَدْحُورًا)"
d-n-r as a single-sense root
its only meaning is the word دِينَار (dīnār), a gold coin
only one sense for the root f-r-t: it denotes sweet, fresh water
al-māʾ al-furāt, glossed simply as al-ʿadhb
a single meaning: something that encloses something else from its sides
**al-jaww, the jaww of the sky**: what arches over the earth on its sides
كُوب (kūb) — a drinking cup or goblet with no handle. Plural: أَكْوَاب (akwāb).
kayfa (كَيْفَ, "how"): a coined interrogative word (kalima mawḍūʿa) used to ask about a person's state or condition
one sound root that indicates pleasantness of taste in a thing
Al-ladhdha (اللَّذَّة) and al-ladhādha (اللَّذَاذَة): the pleasant taste of a thing
a single core meaning: to tarry, linger, or stay put in one place (تَمَكُّث)
لَبِثَ بِالْمَكَانِ (labitha bi-l-makān) — "he stayed / remained in the place,"
لَدُنْ (ladun) — used with the sense of لَدَى (ladā), i.e. عِنْد (ʿind): "at," "with," or "in the presence of."
as two unrelated words
**al-makr** — contrivance and deception (al-iḥtiyāl wa-l-khidāʿ)
He cites Q 28:76: "that of which the mafātiḥ would weigh heavily on the band (al-ʿuṣba)"
a single root whose core sense is agitation and swinging back and forth
causing spoilage or corruption between two parties
نَزَغَ بَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ, "he nazagha among the people,"
al-raḥīq (الرحيق): a name for wine (khamr)
a single core meaning: crumbling/crushing (fatt) combined with twisting (layy)
until it became rufāt, i.e. crumbled fragments or dust
to ask, to question
"In six days" (fī sittati ayyām), Q 7:54
"Sixty poor persons" (sittīna miskīnan), Q 58:4
الوَعْظ (al-waʿẓ): instilling fear or cautioning.
reminding someone of the good, and of that which softens the heart
firmness/stability and constant attachment
al-watīn — a vein constantly attached to the heart, nourishing it — i.e. the aorta
a root (aṣl) that points to thinness in a thing
الزَّيْت (al-zayt), olive oil
